fields.description:
## Why
ADR 0112 decisions 1+2, for the Docker accumulator. At the 2026-09-02 outage
`/var/lib/docker` was 17G (overlay2 16G across 67 layer dirs) while `docker system df`
claimed ~9.5 GB with ZERO dangling images — ~**6.5 GB of orphaned overlay2 invisible to
`docker prune` entirely**. Four prune rounds reclaimed ~1.06 GB against a 29 GB problem. A cap
reading Docker's own accounting cannot see the bytes that caused the outage.

## Design

### One budget, three DIFFERENT enforcement strengths
`infra/scripts/docker-storage-cap.sh` (new) is the single source of truth for a
`/var/lib/docker` budget with an internal split (ADR 0112: "S2 and S5 are one budget, not
two" — writable layers live INSIDE overlay2, so two independent caps are double-counted or
mutually violable). Measured env-settable defaults (decision 6): 20 GiB total, 5 GiB of it
the BuildKit share (today's `BUILD_CACHE_KEEP=5GB`, promoted to one place instead of
duplicated), leaving 15 GiB of image/layer share that S5 sub-divides.

The three parts are NOT equally enforceable and the plan does not pretend otherwise:
1. **BuildKit share (5 GiB) — the daemon's OWN GC**, at the source, on its own schedule:
   `builder.gc` in `/etc/docker/daemon.json`.
2. **Image/layer share (15 GiB) — cap-aware prune** in `autodeploy.sh`, deriving
   `--keep-storage` from the same budget so prune and daemon GC cannot disagree. Docker
   exposes no native total-image ceiling; retention is the supported lever.
3. **Orphaned overlay2 — NEITHER.** Docker does not know those bytes exist, so no cap and no
   prune reaches them. ALARM-ONLY, and that is the point.

### The daemon.json schema is version-dependent, so it is PROBED, not assumed
Engine 25.0 / BuildKit 0.13 introduced `policy[].reservedSpace|maxUsedSpace|minFreeSpace` and
deprecated `defaultKeepStorage` / policy `keepStorage`. The wrong key is silently IGNORED —
the cap would simply not exist. So the script reads the engine version (`docker version
--format '{{.Server.Version}}'`, falling back to `dockerd --version` on first boot, then the
modern schema) and renders what THAT engine honours: `maxUsedSpace` at >= 25.0,
`defaultKeepStorage` below. Both tested via a side-effect-free
`--print-json --engine-version <v>` mode (the `--print-volumes` precedent).

### Install point, and how a LIVE daemon picks it up
The merge goes into `compose-up.sh` **ahead of `systemctl enable --now docker`** (today's
first side-effecting step, line 55), so a first boot starts the daemon with the cap already
in place. On a re-run against a LIVE daemon the write alone is inert, so: the existing
`daemon.json` is BACKED UP and the merged file VALIDATED (`dockerd --validate --config-file`
when available, else a JSON parse); **a failed validation restores the backup and changes
nothing** — a malformed `daemon.json` stops `dockerd` starting, a self-inflicted outage on the
host being protected. Only a validated CHANGE attempts `systemctl reload docker` (SIGHUP); if
that fails the script WARNs loudly naming the runbook step and **does not restart Docker** —
a restart takes Gerrit, the review-bot and MCP down, so it stays an operator decision.

### Detecting the bytes `docker system df` cannot see
Two INDEPENDENT measurements of the same bytes:
- filesystem truth — a bounded `du -sx` over `/var/lib/docker` and one over `.../overlay2`
  (`-x` does not cross into a mounted `overlay2/*/merged`; one `du` run counts a file
  hardlinked across layers once);
- Docker's ledger — `docker system df` images + containers + build cache, human sizes parsed.

`docker_unaccounted_bytes` = overlay2 truth − ledger, clamped at 0. Some divergence is
NORMAL: `du` counts allocated blocks including per-layer directory and whiteout overhead,
while the ledger reports layer sizes with sharing accounted differently. So the threshold is
not "any divergence": 2 GiB, an order of magnitude above that overhead on a 16 GiB tree and
far below the 6.5 GB that went unnoticed — a terraform literal operators retune.

## Metrics (`rebar/host`, dimensionless, 5-min probe)
`docker_storage_bytes`, `docker_storage_used_percent`, `docker_buildkit_cache_bytes`,
`docker_buildkit_cache_used_percent`, `docker_unaccounted_bytes` — published ONLY on a
successful measurement. A failed/timed-out probe publishes nothing and
`treat_missing_data = "breaching"` pages (observability.sh 2e's gated-publish rule), so a
broken probe never reads as a healthy 0.

## Alarms — three, none implying another
1. `rebar-docker-storage-cap-high` — the whole budget saturating.
2. `rebar-docker-buildkit-cache-high` — the BuildKit GENERATOR at its own cap. BuildKit at
   100% of its 5 GiB share is invisible inside a 20 GiB budget reading 60%; a runaway image
   set saturates the budget while BuildKit sits at 10%. The 3e92 argument: alarm on the
   generator, not only on aggregate fullness.
3. `rebar-docker-unaccounted-overlay2` — orphaned bytes above 2 GiB. 1 and 2 say "how full";
   only this says "full of what prune cannot touch", changing remediation from "prune harder"
   (the measured ~1.06 GB failure) to a daemon-level reclaim.

All three: `period=300`/`evaluation_periods=3`/`datapoints_to_alarm=2`,
`treat_missing_data = "breaching"`, `alarm_actions` + `ok_actions` on
`aws_sns_topic.alerts`, pinned BY NAME in `tests/unit/test_alarm_actions_terraform.py`'s
watched set (anti-vacuity floors raised).

## Scope
Out: gate scratch (S1), journald (S3), `/var/tmp` (S4), writable-layer sub-cap (S5).
Terraform written + validated only, never applied.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `docker-storage-cap.sh` holds the whole `/var/lib/docker` budget and its BuildKit/image
      split in ONE place, with measured env-settable defaults and a side-effect-free print
      mode; no cap constant duplicated elsewhere.
- [ ] The rendered `builder.gc` matches the ENGINE VERSION — `maxUsedSpace` at >= 25.0,
      `defaultKeepStorage` below — both covered by tests.
- [ ] `compose-up.sh` merges ahead of `systemctl enable --now docker`, backing up and
      validating first; a validation failure restores the backup and changes nothing; a
      validated change on a live daemon reloads and never auto-restarts.
- [ ] `autodeploy.sh` derives `--keep-storage` from the same budget; tagged rollback images
      (`:prev`, per-release mcp tags) survive a blanket prune.
- [ ] Observability publishes the five metrics, `docker_unaccounted_bytes` being `du` truth
      minus `docker system df`; a failed probe publishes nothing.

- [ ] Terraform declares the three alarms, SNS-wired, breaching, pinned by name;
      `terraform fmt -check -recursive` and `validate` pass.
- [ ] The runbook documents per-generator diagnosis/remediation, the operator restart step
      for a changed `daemon.json`, and forbids deletion under `/var/lib/docker`.
- [ ] Portability: host config plus local script tests; no CI-provider-specific trigger.

## Testing
RED-first: each test below is written and observed FAILING before implementation.
- `pytest -q tests/scripts/test_docker_storage_cap.py` — budget/split derivation,
  per-engine-version `builder.gc` rendering, idempotent merge preserving pre-existing daemon
  keys, backup-restore on a rejected config.
- `pytest -q tests/scripts/test_observability_docker_storage.py` — metric emission over
  stubbed `docker`/`du`, human-size parsing, the unaccounted delta reproducing the incident's
  16G-vs-9.5G shape, silence (not 0) on probe failure.
- `pytest -q tests/unit/test_autodeploy_prune.py` — one budget drives `--keep-storage`;
  rollback images survive.
- `pytest -q tests/unit/test_alarm_actions_terraform.py` — three alarms present, actioned,
  breaching, inside the raised floors.
(all run as `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" pytest …`)
- `terraform fmt -check -recursive infra/terraform`; `terraform -chdir=infra/terraform init
  -backend=false && … validate`.
- `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the three gates invisible to lint:
  `test_mechanism_delta.py`, `test_predates_gate_guard_parity.py`, `test_api_surface_gate.py`.
